questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from specific lanes. A green arrow:

options.text: Is used only on one-way streets.
Means you can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
Means you may proceed only if a circular green light is also showing.
Points the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: Means you can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. You must turn in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road curves right and then left. Slow down to safely navigate these curves.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Keep more distance between you and the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep more distance between you and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: Keep more space between your car and the one ahead when it is dark. Use your headlights to see better. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights because the bright light can blind you.

questions.question: You may pass a vehicle when:

options.text: You are on a hill or curve.
There is a solid line next to your lane.
There is a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross into the other lane to pass. A solid line means you cannot pass. Only pass when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep driving at your current speed.
A traffic light is coming up.

questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic light is coming up.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic light is ahead.

questions.question: If an edge line angles inward on a road, it means:

options.text: The speed limit is going down.
The speed limit is going up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is getting narrower.
questions.explanation: When an edge line angles inward, the road ahead is narrowing. Merge safely into the correct lane.

questions.question: To be ready for anything on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Look at the whole road and the sides of the road at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus only on the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the whole road and the sides of the road at all times.
questions.explanation: You need to look at the whole road, including the sides. This helps you see and avoid problems before they happen.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines down the center of a road mean passing is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. No one can pass from either side.

questions.question: You may never park:

options.text: Within 50 feet of a fire hydrant.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a crosswalk.
questions.explanation: You cannot park in a crosswalk. You also cannot park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. Your car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:
questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water sits on the road. Most tires work well up to 35 mph. Above 35 mph, tires cannot push water away. Your tires may lose grip and slide on the water like water skis.

questions.question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the other driver will keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even if you signal, do not assume that other drivers will give you space or let you pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: You may drive across a dashed white line:

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross these lines to pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: At a red traffic light with a green arrow, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow if:

options.text: You first come to a complete stop.
You wait until the light changes.
You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If you are in a lane with a green arrow and the road is clear, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow. This applies whether the arrow appears alone or with other signals.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: A stop sign is shaped like a(n):
questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon.
questions.explanation: Only stop signs have an octagon shape. All eight-sided signs tell drivers to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: Which of the following affects how alcohol impacts you?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
How much time passes between drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: All three choices
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, time between drinks, and your weight. Eating can slow alcohol absorption but cannot prevent intoxication if you drink too much.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: At dusk or on overcast days, you must turn on your headlights. Use low beam when within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or 500 feet of a vehicle ahead. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the left.
Passing is allowed from the right.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean no passing is allowed from either side.

questions.question: One strategy of defensive driving is:

options.text: Looking straight ahead as you drive.
Staying alert and keeping your eyes moving.
Expecting other drivers to make up for your mistakes.
Being sure you can avoid danger at the last moment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staying alert and keeping your eyes moving.
questions.explanation: Traffic conditions change constantly. Scan the road ahead, notice what is happening to the sides, and check your mirrors every few seconds.
